# Living screencast recipe

A walkthrough staged like a real screen recording: a calm window floating over a warm wallpaper, a camera that auto-zooms to follow the cursor, and a mascot built from big square pixels that lives inside the crisp interface and acts out what the software does.

## Concept

- Opening: a small dark window (chat or terminal) grows while its messages type in. The mascot appears inside it, hops out onto its top edge, and the dark window melts into the bright app.
- Nothing is recorded. Windows, chips, fields and buttons are all rebuilt in HTML/CSS. That frees the camera to travel anywhere, and type remains crisp at any zoom.
- Two actors, never a hand. Cursor = the user. Mascot = the software. The look comes from two resolutions colliding: a hard-edged pixel sprite on smooth anti-aliased UI.
- Cause and effect: each mascot action produces a real UI change (it stomps a button, the button locks). Each user action appears as a cursor move, a click, or a key on the HUD.
- Wrong direction: a dark stage talk (black stage, abstract invented UI); a pixel-art game (the world is vector UI, only mascot and props are pixels); a true capture. The UI belongs to the subject: invented but coherent labels, believable states, no lorem ipsum.

## Build

- Window: one browser or app window, about 62 % of frame width, 20 px corners, hairline plus soft two-layer shadow. It floats on a wallpaper of 2-3 big soft radial glows over the background. Slim menu bar across the top. Window title bar: three traffic-light dots and a rounded address pill.
- Pixel grid is strict. Mascot = 18 x 10 square pixels, 9 px each at 1920. Props ("!" bubble, sparks, "z", check mark, dust) share that grid with crisp edges (`shape-rendering: crispEdges`). Snap mascot position to half a pixel (4.5 px) so motion steps.
- Ground = the top edge of a real element: heading letters, chip, input, button, progress bar. Never stand elsewhere. Read coordinates from the live DOM with `getBoundingClientRect`; no hand-placed numbers.
- Depth only where it directs attention: a vignette spotlight on the single figure worth remembering. Never blur text meant to be read. No filters on the world.
- Overlays are neutral frosted pills: chapter pill top left, caption bottom centre, key HUD bottom right. Nothing more on screen.

## Palette

- `--latar`: wallpaper ground. `--latar-2`: window surface. Cards, chips and fields inside the window sit on `--latar` with a hairline mixed from `--teks`.
- `--utama`: the mascot and every "this changed" fill (selected chip, locked button, filled bar segments, scene change). The mascot must be the most saturated item in any frame, so the rest of the UI stays neutral.
- `--aksen`: tints one wallpaper glow and the "!" outline, nothing else. `--aksen-di-latar` and `--utama-di-latar` colour caption keywords, the big figure and contact details.
- Fixed: traffic-light dots, check-mark green, the mascot's shaded belly row (a darker mix of `--utama`), mascot eyes in `--teks-di-utama` so they read on any brand colour.

## Type

- `--font-judul`: Playfair Display 700 for the in-world title and the big figure. 210 px title, 76 px page heading, 280 px figure. A restrained serif keeps the UI feeling like an editorial app; any brand headline font will do.
- `--font-isi`: Inter 400/600 at 26-36 px for UI text (labels, buttons; captions 28 px).
- IBM Plex Mono for the address pill, chapter pill, day times and key HUD.
- Titles stay diegetic: a page heading or confirmation message, never a floating overlay.

## Timing

- Jump: crouch 0.14 s (squash 0.3), take-off stretch 0.1 s (scaleY 1.18), arc in two halves (`power2.out` rising, `power2.in` falling), landing squash 0.07 s, elastic settle 0.35 s. Six dust pixels spread 30-90 px and fade over 0.45 s.
- Walk: x/y stay on the half-pixel grid; legs swap every 0.16 s; 0.5 s per hop across one chip. Eyes do the acting: glance right when the cursor is right, widen on surprise, happy arcs on success, closed when asleep. Arms up to cheer.
- Cursor: eased path 0.6-1.0 s (`power2.inOut`), 0.14 s press (scale 0.8) on click. It never teleports.
- UI responds like real software: chip fills in 0.2 s, input ring fades in 0.15 s, typing one letter per 0.12 s, button presses to 90 % height and releases.
- Scene change is never a cut. Old window shrinks to 70 % and slides out 760 px in 0.7 s (`power2.inOut`) while the next grows from 70 % in its place. The camera first pulls back to 1x and the mascot hops across. The opening may melt instead: the small dark window fades out as the bright page fades in over it.
- Last scene holds still 2 s or more.

## Camera

A single unbroken take inside the screen. Zoom stays within 1-1.5; clamp the centre so the frame never reveals area beyond the monitor. No cuts, no wipes: a window shrinks away and the next grows in.
- Push to the title, 1.3x over 1.1 s: "this is where it begins". App name, channel intro.
- Push to the cursor target, 1.35-1.45x: "this is where it happens". Picking a slot, filling a field, a setting.
- Follow the mascot along a bar or list, 1.5x, linear: software working through items. Counting, scanning, a checklist.
- Push plus vignette freeze, 1.5-1.7x: the one figure to remember. A total, guarantee, price.
- Pull back to the full window, 1x: the whole result. Summary, confirmation.
- Slow drift when idle: the app feels alive during a narration line.

Rules: never zoom out past 1. Never put a caption over what it discusses. Keep the mascot off any text the viewer must read; leave a gap over the element it stands on.

## Signature moves

- Diegetic title: the name is a real page heading; the mascot drops from above and lands on its letters on a downbeat. For: a booking page, a channel's welcome page, a class portal, a story title card.
- Top-edge walk: the mascot paces the top edges of a row of controls, eyes tracking, while the cursor chooses. For: choosing a time slot, a size, a recipe step, a lesson chapter.
- Stomp the button: the mascot jumps on the submit button at the moment of the cursor click; the button presses and changes state. For: sending a form, publishing a post, exporting a video, paying.
- Moving floor: the mascot rides the end of a progress bar or list, filling it as a figure counts up. For: this week's sales, followers gained, lessons finished, chapters written.
- Spotlight freeze: push in and darken the edges around the one number carrying the promise. For: "9 of 12 booked", a deadline, a guarantee, a price.
- Sleepy ending: the mascot lands on the confirmation heading and dozes while the contact card holds. For: a booked slot, saved draft, enrolled student, finished chapter.

## Avoid

- Invented features. Each label and state must make sense inside its own made-up UI.
- Mascot hovering or sliding away from its element. Measure the DOM and stand on top edges only.
- A mascot covering text or sitting under the caption. Reserve a gap above the element it stands on.
- Blur or zoom-out: rack-blur on text to be read, zoom below 1.
- A hand, arm or finger anywhere on screen; the cursor stands in for the user.
- Mixed pixel sizes in the sprite. Every sprite pixel is the same size, grid-snapped, scaled only by the camera.
- Photographic wallpaper or busy backdrops. Keep glows soft so window and mascot own the frame.
- Reusing a source film's product, UI or story. Write your own subject.

# Living screencast: beat plan

Default length 15 s. Tempo per beat (seconds): short 2.4, medium 3.8, long 5.2.

## hook

- en: the title as a real UI heading in a floating window; the pixel mascot drops in and lands on its letters with a squash and dust
- id: judul jadi judul halaman di jendela mengambang; maskot piksel jatuh dan mendarat di huruf judul dengan penyet dan debu

## problem

- en: the messy state shown in the window: the cursor hunts, the mascot stands on the stuck element, sweating, eyes darting; caption names it
- id: keadaan berantakan tampil di jendela: kursor mencari-cari, maskot berdiri di elemen yang macet, mata bergerak; caption menyebutnya

## fact

- en: push-in on one UI element; the mascot stands on its top edge, eyes on it, a frosted caption pill under the window
- id: zoom ke satu elemen antarmuka; maskot berdiri di tepi atasnya, mata menatapnya, caption kaca di bawah jendela

## step

- en: the cursor clicks, the mascot walks the top edges to the next control and stomps it; a key HUD shows the typing; one step per move
- id: kursor mengklik, maskot menyusuri tepi atas ke kontrol berikutnya dan menginjaknya; tuts tampil di HUD; satu langkah satu gerakan

## compare

- en: two windows side by side, the old way and the new; the mascot hops from one to the other and cheers over the faster one
- id: dua jendela berdampingan, cara lama dan baru; maskot melompat dari satu ke yang lain dan bersorak di atas yang lebih cepat

## number

- en: a giant figure counts up as the mascot walks a segmented bar, filling each segment; vignette and push-in freeze on the total
- id: angka besar naik saat maskot menyusuri batang bersegmen dan mengisinya; vinyet dan zoom menahan angka akhir

## proof

- en: a message or review lands in the window; the mascot rides it in on its top edge, then cheers with sparks as the cursor approves
- id: pesan atau ulasan masuk ke jendela; maskot menumpanginya dari tepi atas, lalu bersorak dengan percikan saat kursor menyetujui

## offer

- en: the offer as a card in the UI: the cursor hovers its button, the mascot waves on top, a caption names the price
- id: penawaran jadi kartu di antarmuka: kursor melayang di tombolnya, maskot melambai di atas, caption menyebut harganya

## cta

- en: a confirmation page: the mascot lands on the heading and falls asleep; the contact card rises and holds still for 2 s
- id: halaman konfirmasi: maskot mendarat di judul lalu tertidur; kartu kontak naik dan diam 2 detik

## payoff

- en: the finished result on screen, window calm; the mascot lands on it, eyes shut happy, one caption line; held 2 s
- id: hasil jadi di layar, jendela tenang; maskot mendarat di atasnya, mata terpejam senang, satu baris caption; diam 2 detik
